author: k. b. ramos
title: Lauren Stebbins named finalist for NCEA YETI Workhorse Award
text:
Baylor equestrian’s Lauren Stebbins was named a finalist for the National Collegiate Equestrian Association’s (NCEA) YETI Workhorse Award, the association announced on Apr. 13.
The NCEA YETI Workhorse Award recognizes a teammate who exemplifies dedication, support, and positive influence within their team. The award is given to an athlete who has made a significant impact by fostering teamwork and upholding the values of their program.
Stebbins, a fifth-year senior from Atlanta, Georgia, concluded her collegiate career with an 8-5 record in the Flat event. During the 2024-25 season she posted a 6-4 record and followed with a 2-1 mark in the 2025-26 season. She achieved her career-best high score of 88 during the semifinals of the Big 12 Equestrian Championship against Oklahoma State in 2025. This past season, Stebbins earned her first Most Outstanding Performer honor after winning her point against Fresno State with a score of 82.50-82.
In addition to her athletic accomplishments, Stebbins serves as president of Baylor’s Student-Athlete Advisory Committee (SAAC), where she works to provide leadership opportunities for fellow student-athletes. She has also received Baylor equestrian’s “Sic ‘Em Award” for three consecutive years—a recognition from coaches for unwavering commitment to both Baylor University and its equestrian program.
Other finalists for this year’s NCEA YETI Workhorse Award include Stevie Brown from UT Martin, Kinsey Cooper from Georgia, and Ava Peck from Southern Methodist University (SMU). The winner will be announced Wednesday night at the NCEA National Championship.
